suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-12 adds this draft-primary relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. The review describes chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) as an under-diagnosed complication of acute pulmonary embolism caused by incomplete embolus resolution and specifies perfusion, imaging, anticoagulation-interval, and right-heart-catheterization diagnostic elements. Restrict the broad pulmonary-hypertension target to separately established chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension after a documented pulmonary embolism. Require persistent mismatched perfusion or chronic thromboembolic/fibrotic obstruction after an appropriate post-PE anticoagulation interval and hemodynamically confirmed pulmonary hypertension under accepted criteria. Do not infer CTEPH from acute PE, persistent dyspnea, hypoxemia, or an echocardiographic estimate alone. Preserve left-heart disease, other lung disease or hypoxia, chronic thromboembolic disease without pulmonary hypertension, drugs/toxins, and other pulmonary-hypertension etiologies as competing explanations. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of pulmonary-embolism and pulmonary-hypertension
Chronology compatible with the approved bounded proposition
Phenotype/claim boundary: phenotype-restricted chronic thromboembolic complication after pulmonary embolism
Assessment of competing etiologies and treatment/context confounders
